app.title: qPCR Fold-Change Analyzer
app.summary: A person loads well-level Ct values from a table or a qPCR instrument export, matches the columns, and assigns samples to groups. They pick a control group, a normalisation strategy (reference genes, a spike-in, or the global mean of all assays), and QC thresholds. They then check technical replicates and sample quality, exclude bad samples, and confirm that the reference genes are stable. Finally they read fold changes and statistics against the control, tune a publication figure, and download it along with draft methods and results text and an Excel report. Two side tools estimate sample sizes for the next study and fit amplification efficiency from a dilution series.

task.text: Turn raw qPCR Ct values into quality-checked, normalised fold changes per group with statistics, a figure and draft write-up text.

data.text: Well-level qPCR cycle-threshold values, one row per well, with sample, group, target assay and technical replicate. The data arrives as a generic table or an instrument results export.
data.item: a technical-replicate well: one sample measured for one target assay

stage.text: analysing qPCR results after the run, from quality control through to fold changes ready for the manuscript

mechanism.text: The page runs top to bottom: import and column matching, then settings, then a row of result tabs that all recompute from the same chosen normaliser, control group and exclusions. Quality-check tabs flag samples that the person then excludes in a multiselect, and every table, figure and paragraph downstream updates.

field.text: relative quantification of qPCR (ΔΔCt) for miRNA in molecular biology

workflow.name: turn raw measurements into normalised group comparisons with quality checks and a written report

steps.here: Choose an example or upload a CSV, TXT or Excel instrument export. Header lines and NTC or standard wells are dropped automatically. Then match the Sample, Group, Target and Ct columns, or edit groups guessed from sample names.

Pick the control group and the group order, choose reference-gene, spike-in or global-mean normalisation and its assays, and set the replicate SD, late-Ct, hemolysis and spike-in thresholds, the statistical test, the correction and per-assay efficiencies.

Replicate sets are flagged for high SD, late Ct or no amplification, and the outlying replicate is optionally dropped. Samples are flagged by a hemolysis ΔCq and by spike-in drift from the median. Flagged samples can be excluded, and every result recomputes.

steps.step: check that the reference measure is sound
steps.here: geNorm M ranks the candidate reference genes by stepwise elimination, with a table and plot of raw Ct by group. The person is warned when the chosen references differ from the most stable pair.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Efficiency-corrected ΔΔCt gives per-sample fold changes, then geometric-mean fold change with a 95% CI per group, then each group against the control on the log2 scale with multiple-testing correction.

Grouped bar figure with options for scale, error bars, points and stars, downloadable as PNG, SVG or PDF. The methods and results paragraphs and the reference list are drafted from the settings and the statistics.
One Excel workbook holds the settings, group summary, statistics, per-sample results, QC, hemolysis, spike-in, reference stability, the drafted text and the input data.

distinctive: Three interchangeable normalisation strategies (reference genes, exogenous spike-in, global mean of the assays detected in every sample), and every result follows the one chosen
Sample-quality screens for circulating material: a hemolysis ratio between two marker assays with high-risk and borderline thresholds, and spike-in recovery against the median
Reference-gene stability ranking (geNorm M) that warns when the chosen normalisers are not the most stable pair
Methods and results paragraphs drafted in manuscript language from the actual settings and adjusted p-values, with citations
A sample-size planner that uses the variance in the person's own data, and a standard-curve calculator for assay efficiency that feeds the efficiency table
